clue.text: Left in to take part in the contest though quite done

indicators.note: the first 'in' tells us the letter for left goes inside the verb phrase that follows

parts.words: to take part in the contest
parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest

explanation.surface: A competitor who has left is drawn back into a contest that was already over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete is entirely finished, so quite done is a synonym.

clue.text: He preaches heaven to a religious clique

definitions.text: He preaches heaven to a religious clique

parts.words: He preaches heaven to a religious clique
parts.note: a slang term for a clergyman, especially a military chaplain, who guides souls heavenward as one might steer through the air

explanation.surface: A preacher promises paradise to a small sect of believers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a clergyman or chaplain, one whose job is to steer people towards heaven.

clue.text: A news clipping from the vegetable catalogue?

parts.note: a par is journalists' slang for a short news paragraph, a single news item
a snip is a small piece cut off, a clipping

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a short item out of a seed catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' and 'catalogue?' are surface dressing: the question mark flags the playful idea of a news cutting taken from a list of vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root crop related to the carrot, one example of a vegetable.

clue.text: Fate of a skit composed about the Middle East

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rearranged letters surround the region's abbreviation
composed means put together anew, so the letters of skit are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch written about the Middle East meets a certain fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate of' reads as if the sketch has a fate; 'Fate' alone is the definition and 'of a' are link words, so the A is not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, a word borrowed from Turkish and Arabic for one's allotted lot.

clue.text: One who loses weight more quickly

definitions.meaning: someone who goes without food, and so slims
the comparative of fast, meaning at greater speed

explanation.definitionFit: One who abstains from eating sheds pounds; the comparative adjective means with greater speed.

clue.text: Big letters provide lots of big buildings around big town

indicators.note: around tells us the plural word for buildings is wrapped about the word for the main city

parts.note: blocks are large buildings, as in office or tower blocks
a capital is a country's principal city

explanation.surface: Enormous signage spells out a city skyline of tower blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are the large upper-case forms of the alphabet, the big letters used for emphasis.

clue.text: Juggle successfully with one's available cash

definitions.meaning: read literally, to keep things balanced in one's hand while juggling
the money left over and ready to use, a surplus held

explanation.definitionFit: Literally keeping things steady in the hand while juggling; also an accounting term for money remaining unspent.

clue.text: High mass for world leaders?

parts.note: not a church service but a top-level gathering of heads of state, high being the peak and mass being a crowd

explanation.surface: A grand church service is laid on for presidents and prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A conference between heads of government at the very highest level, a summit being a peak.

clue.text: Propagated cutting now growing despite a blunder

parts.note: a slip is a cutting taken from a plant for propagation
up means rising, as a plant growing upwards

explanation.surface: A gardener's cutting is thriving in spite of a mistake in taking it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a minor mistake or error, a blunder.

clue.text: It doesn't matter when for quite a while

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a fair stretch of time

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means at an unspecified moment; split in two it means a considerable period.

clue.text: Boy reluctant to leave Lothian

indicators.note: to leave means the synonym for reluctant departs from the place name

parts.note: loth (or loath) means unwilling, reluctant

explanation.surface: A lad is unwilling to move away from his home region of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Lothian is a region of Scotland around Edinburgh; 'to leave' removes LOTH from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Scottish boy's name, so an example of a boy.

clue.text: It sounds a phoney way to pay out

indicators.note: it sounds tells us we want a word heard like another one

parts.note: phoney means fake or unreal

explanation.surface: Someone describes a fraudulent method of making payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay out a rope or line is to let it run off a reel, to unwind it.

clue.text: Spray air stain to get an effect of wood mosaic

indicators.note: spray suggests scattering, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A woodworker uses an airbrush of stain to give a mosaic look.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlaid decorative woodwork in which pieces of differently coloured wood form a picture.

clue.text: Court card which is a court winner

definitions.meaning: a playing card, the one-spot of a suit, loosely grouped with the picture cards
on a tennis court, a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.definitionFit: The highest card in a suit, and in tennis an unreturnable serve that wins the point outright.

clue.text: Tome men reprint? No, just a reminder

indicators.note: to reprint here means to set the letters in type again in a different order

explanation.surface: Should the publisher reissue the old volume? No, a souvenir copy will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or souvenir kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: Won back present

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: A prize is recovered by its winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The present moment is this very instant, the current time.

clue.text: Take upon oneself to provide a page summary

parts.note: a resume is a summary, from the French

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to write a one-page digest.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to venture or take the liberty of doing something without permission.

clue.text: Be seen again to harvest fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a crop
a pear is a common orchard fruit

explanation.surface: Orchard pickers come back to gather the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view, to show up once more after being absent.

clue.text: A bus I rub accidentally on the city fringes

indicators.note: accidentally suggests things knocked out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A commuter brushes against a bus out in the outskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The residential districts on the outskirts of a city, collectively.

clue.text: Changes needed to make viola out of viol

definitions.text: Changes needed to make viola out of viol

parts.words: Changes needed to make viola out of viol
parts.note: turning the old instrument's name into the modern one needs only an extra letter tacked on, an addition at the end

explanation.surface: A luthier asks what alterations convert an old viol into a viola.
explanation.walkthrough: The word viol becomes viola by adding a single letter, so the change needed is an addition.
explanation.definitionFit: Items added at the end of a book or document, supplementary additions.

clue.text: Single gentleman's weapon which true gentlemen should keep

parts.note: one means a single unit
a sword was the weapon carried by a gentleman

explanation.surface: An unmarried man carries a blade, as an honourable gentleman should.
explanation.walkthrough: A man of honour keeps his word, that is, his promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise or pledge, which an honourable person is expected to honour.

clue.text: Appear only to expose faults

definitions.meaning: to reveal someone's shortcomings, to embarrass

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrive somewhere and to reveal another's weakness by contrast.

clue.text: Appeal to a mass meeting in spoken words

parts.note: O is an exclamation used in appeals, as in O Lord
a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: A speaker calls out to a crowd at a big political event.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by mouth, through speech rather than writing.

clue.text: In the morning lost blood so walked slowly

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon
to bleed is to lose blood; the past tense is bled

explanation.surface: Someone wounded early in the day staggered along.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Prince follows his wife for a swim in the sea

indicators.note: follows puts the letter for prince after the name of his spouse

parts.note: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales, wife of Prince Charles

explanation.surface: A royal husband goes in after his wife for a seaside bathe.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a quick plunge or bathe.

clue.text: Era when the French wore clogs to do deliberate damage

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog, the French word for it
an age is an era, a period of history

explanation.surface: A history lesson describes a period when people in France went about in wooden shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is said to come from workers throwing their sabots into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage is to wreck or obstruct something on purpose.

clue.text: Let a woman do what she will with straight hair

definitions.text: a woman do what she will with straight hair
definitions.meaning: read as two words, to give the hair a permanent wave

explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means allow; split, it describes giving straight hair a permanent wave.

clue.text: Ran West London borough by chicanery

parts.note: to double is to run, as soldiers move at the double
Ealing is a borough in west London

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted through a west London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful dealing, acting one way while intending another; trickery.
